title: Anchored straight stitch
subtitle: How to lay a long thread flat and hold it in place with a tiny couching stitch.
excerpt: A long straight stitch tends to loop above the surface of the cloth. Anchoring it with a small couching stitch across its centre keeps it flat and prevents snagging.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Long and short stitch, laid work.
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Couching and laid stitch entries.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small stitch worked across a laid thread to hold it flat against the cloth surface. The laid thread is not pulled through the cloth itself; the couching stitches anchor it from above.

content.text: Any straight stitch longer than about 8 mm will lift above the surface of the cloth and snag if not anchored. A
over the centre of a long straight stitch holds it flat without distorting the main stitch.

items.name: Stranded cotton, 2 strands for the main stitch, 1 strand for anchoring

content.text: Work the main straight stitch at the desired length, but do not pull it tight.
Bring a second needle threaded with a finer thread up at the midpoint of the main stitch.
Make a tiny stitch (1 to 2 mm wide) across the main thread, going back into the cloth on the other side.
Pull the couching stitch snug, not tight: it should hold the main thread flat without dimpling it.
For very long stitches, add anchoring stitches every 8 to 10 mm along the length.

items.symptom: The anchoring stitch is visible and detracts from the main stitch
items.cause: The anchoring stitch thread is the same weight as the main stitch.
items.fix: Use one strand for anchoring when the main stitch uses two or more. Match the colour of the anchoring thread to the cloth if the stitch is part of a fill.

items.symptom: The main stitch still lifts despite anchoring
items.cause: Only one anchoring point was used for a very long stitch.
items.fix: Add anchoring stitches every 8 to 10 mm for stitches longer than 2 cm.

content.text: Anchored straight stitch is the basis of all laid work and couching techniques in surface embroidery and Goldwork.
is also how metallic thread is applied in goldwork: the stiff metal thread is laid on the surface and couched down with fine matching thread.
